problem_found: The normalizing verifier accepted clean wood grain as floor_stain.
The normalizing verifier accepted the 3.0s vanity observation even though its own explanation said missing_hardware was not supported.
Normalization therefore needs to preserve the original defect category/core physical class rather than merely preserve a nearby visible mark.
normalization_rule: Unsupported descriptive details may be removed.
Normalization must not change the physical defect into another category or defect class.
A stain cannot become missing hardware; a crack cannot rescue a droplet; a generic mark cannot rescue a hardware claim.
benign_alternative_rule: For stains/discoloration, explicitly compare against normal material variation, wood grain, knots, lighting, shadows, and reflections.
For hardware claims, explicitly compare against stain, surface mark, ordinary fastener, and unrelated damage.
Accept only when the original defect category is better supported than the strongest competing explanation.

diagnostic_cases.reason: Normal wood grain/material variation should be the stronger explanation.
Exposed mounting hole supports the original hardware/mounting-damage class; screw-head detail may be removed.
Visible dark mark does not establish missing hardware.
